=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18487-18529 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The re-plan path in `_plan_auto_approval_gate` runs `gh issue edit --add-label 'ai:planning' --remove-label 'ai:awaiting-approval'`, posts the `/answer` comment and calls `phase_cap_note_dispatch "ai:planning"`, but it never calls `phase_cap_can_dispatch "ai:planning" "automation_path_replan" "${issue_num}"`; its callers (the auto_approve and retrigger_implement arms) only check the `ai:implementing` cap, through `phase_cap_state_for_action` (lines 17015-17031), at lines 18623 and 23256.
  WHY: With PHASE_CAPS_ENABLED=true and ai:planning at its limit, every eligible held issue in a tick is still re-planned and pushes PHASE_CAPS_RUNNING_BY_STATE["ai:planning"] past the configured limit; reviewers disagreed on severity (MAJOR from sonnet, gemini, minimax and luna; NIT from glm, which calls it "Governance-cap inconsistency, no data risk"), so the highest, MAJOR→high, is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18509-18527 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The label edit to `ai:planning` runs before the marker comment POST and the two steps are not atomic, so if the POST fails (`outcome=replan_comment_failed`) the issue sits in `ai:planning` with no `<!-- ai:automation-path-replan:v1 issue=N -->` marker, and the `retrigger_plan` arm (lines 18692-18708 / 18695-18702; standalone 23343-23357) then posts a plain `/answer` that carries no marker.
  WHY: If the retriggered plan is held again, the marker check (lines 18493-18502) finds nothing, so a second automatic re-plan runs (minimax says a third is possible too); this breaks the documented "at most one label edit and one comment per issue" / "one re-plan per issue" contract; reviewers disagreed on severity (MAJOR from minimax, raised as both an error-path and a concurrency finding; NIT from sonnet, gemini, luna and glm, with sonnet and glm noting it is bounded and needs a failed POST), so the highest, MAJOR→high, is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18513-18517 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The re-plan `/answer` body (`gate_replan_body`) has no `[auto-answered-by-orchestrator]` marker, but `.github/workflows/plan.yml` lines 42-49 require that marker on a Bot-authored `/answer` when `AI_PIPELINE_APPROVER_LOGIN` is configured.
  WHY: The issue moves to `ai:planning` but plan.yml skips the trigger, so the re-plan never starts; reviewers disagreed on severity (BLOCKER from gemini and minimax, MAJOR from luna), so the highest, BLOCKER→critical, is used; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly dispute this finding as a false positive: per plan.yml:29-40/33-39, a User-type OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR plain `/answer` is accepted only when the marker is absent, retrigger_plan (lines 18697, 23346) already posts plain `/answer` under the same GH_PAT identity, and adding the marker could reject the comment.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18511 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `replan_label_failed` branch has no `return 1`; it echoes the log line and falls through to the hold notice (`_plan_auto_approval_hold_notify`, line 18533), with no explicit retry and no way to hold back the notice until the edit succeeds.
  WHY: A transient label-edit failure sends the hold notice while the issue stays in `ai:awaiting-approval`; the next tick retries, so it is recoverable, but the advertised early-return guard is only a fall-through.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18525 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `replan_comment_failed` branch logs `outcome=replan_comment_failed` and returns 1 without emitting `STALL_SKIP reason=automation_path_plan_hold`.
  WHY: Stall-judge and the wave dashboard count held issues from STALL_SKIP lines, so telemetry reports one fewer held issue than reality and the re-plan layer is invisible to them.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18509-18520 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The direct `gh issue edit` label mutation (add `ai:planning`, remove `ai:awaiting-approval`) is a stall-recovery side effect whose §14 audit comment exists only at the call site, and the edit happens before the marker comment is on the issue.
  WHY: On a partial failure, an operator sees `ai:planning` arrive with no matching `ai:automation-path-replan:v1` comment, and nothing on the issue explains the transition.
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py:1591-1627 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_plan_gate_replannable_absent_for_every_other_reason` fills `seen = set()` with `seen.add(reason)` but never asserts `seen` against the ten expected reason strings.
  WHY: A dropped, merged or duplicate case still passes, which weakens the issue's "one case per listed reason" regression contract; the fix is to assert seen == {"untrusted_author", "no_allowlist", "malformed_allowlist", "workflow_edits_disabled", "grant_issue_mismatch", "automation_path_plan_auto_approval_disabled", "origin_unverified", "plan_too_large_for_grant", "plan_files_outside_files_touched", "plan_gate_error"}.
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py:1563-1579 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The new tests (and other test files) are claimed to cause CI failures: `ruff`, `shellcheck`, `test_files_touched_scope_guard.py`.
  WHY: The PR is said to be failing pre-push checks, which would mean a broken implementation or verification; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash could not map these failures to any code in the diff, and glm's static trace did not reproduce them.
- (external check, unmapped to diff):n/a | severity=low | confidence=3

  PROBLEM: The only failed check-run, `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` on head SHA fc228c4 (run 41404143584), died with `custom_instructions_too_large` before reviewing any code; separately, the untrusted pre-push-gate report in the PR description claims 4 failures (tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py, ruff, shellcheck) that no check-run at the head SHA confirms.
  WHY: Neither is shown to be caused by this diff; both need a real test/lint run to resolve rather than a code edit.

  WHY: A re-held plan finds no marker (lines 18493-18502), so a second automatic re-plan runs and breaks "at most one label edit and one comment per issue"; the impact is bounded and low.
